meta.reference: Maass, C. and Schumann, U. (1994). Numerical simulation of turbulent flow over a wavy boundary. In: Voke, P. R., Kleiser, L. and Chollet, J.-P. (eds.), Direct and Large-Eddy Simulation I, Fluid Mechanics and Its Applications 26, Kluwer, Dordrecht, 287-297.
meta.doi_note: The scanned PDF shows no DOI; the DOI is the Springer chapter link of this title (book 10.1007/978-94-011-1000-6, chapter 25, pp. 287-297), checked on link.springer.com on 6 Oct 2026.
meta.experiment: Hudson, J. D. (1993). The effect of a wavy boundary on turbulent flow. PhD thesis, Dept. Chemical Engineering, University of Illinois, Urbana (LDV in a water channel; no DOI). A later DNS of the same Hudson flow: Cherukat, P., Na, Y., Hanratty, T. J. and McLaughlin, J. B. (1998), Theor. Comput. Fluid Dyn. 11, 109-134, https://doi.org/10.1007/s001620050083
meta.case: Plane channel, flat no-slip top wall at z = H, lower wall h(x) = delta cos(2 pi x / lambda); delta = 0.05 H, lambda = H; Re = Um H / nu = 4780; Lx x Ly x H = 4 x 2 x 1; periodic in x, y; Um held constant by a mean pressure gradient; DNS. Hudson's channel: H = 50.8 mm, delta = 2.54 mm, lambda = 50.8 mm, Um = 86.4 mm/s (water).
meta.coordinates: x/lambda = 0 at a wave crest. z/H = 0 at the mean surface (crest +0.05, trough -0.05). eta = H (z - h)/(H - h) is the paper's terrain-following coordinate (eta = 0 on the wavy wall, eta = H at the top wall).
meta.normalisation: Velocities and variances (Figs. 2, 6) are normalised with the mean velocity of the LOWER HALF of the channel, both for the simulation and for the experiment (paper p. 291); the paper's simulated lower-half mean was 7 % below the whole-channel Um. Fig. 7 uses Um and rho Um^2.
meta.averaging: Paper: case 4 at t = 60 H/Um, averaged over y and over the 4 waves (no time average; Figs. 2, 3, 6, 7). Hudson: time averages over 60 s = 102 H/Um.
meta.digitisation: Digitised on 6 Oct 2026 from the scanned figures rendered at 300 dpi (pdftoppm), axis calibration on the tick marks; curves traced by a pixel tracker, open circles by ring template matching, then checked by eye and filtered. Uncertainty: about +-0.01 in the plotted quantity for Fig. 7a, +-3 % of full scale for Figs. 6 and 7b, +-0.03 Um in u and +-0.005 H in z for Fig. 2 (larger next to the wall, where markers overlap; near-wall parts of the simulated profiles are not digitised). Hudson's points in Fig. 2 are a subset of the markers shown. Figs. 2 and 6 and the drag numbers were redone on 6 Oct 2026 (evening): see the digitisation and note fields of those entries.

table1.note: Friction velocities from the total drag (paper p. 296): wavy wall = form + skin.

scalars.separation_note: Paper: separated region (bounded by Psi = 0) from x/lambda = 0.2 to 0.63, an interval 0.2 longer than in the experiment, and about 60 % higher. The experiment's end points are not given; 0.23 = 0.43 - 0.2 is derived.
scalars.pressure_max_note: Coincides with reattachment (paper p. 294); the simulated maximum is about 30 % below the experimental value.
scalars.drag_note: Total: Table I, u_tau,wa = 0.101 -> 0.0102 Um^2 (Fig. 7b at eta = 0: 0.0101-0.0103). Friction: paper p. 295-296, the frictional flux at the flat wall (0.070^2 = 0.0049, Table I) is 34 % higher than at the wavy wall -> 0.0049/1.34 = 0.0037. Pressure: total - friction = 0.0065; Fig. 7b (dotted, 600 dpi) reads 0.0060-0.0063 at eta = 0.02; 0.0063 +- 0.0003 is used. The earlier file had skin 0.0044 (from total - pressure with a coarse reading).
scalars.uu_max_note: Paper p. 293: the u-variance maxima are 0.05 H from the upper and 0.09 H from the lower wall (the earlier file had the two swapped).

fig2_u_profiles.quantity: u / Um_lower vs z/H at x/lambda = 0.0, 0.1, ..., 0.9
fig2_u_profiles.units: u: Um_lower; z: H (z = 0 at the mean surface)
fig2_u_profiles.format: sim_case4: [z/H, u/Um_lower] along the curve from the top (z = 0.48) to the wall, in path order (not sorted: near the wall in the trough the curve is not single-valued in z); exp_hudson: [z/H, u/Um_lower] of each LDV circle, sorted by z.
fig2_u_profiles.digitisation: Re-digitised 6 Oct 2026 (evening) at 600 dpi: x/lambda calibrated on the 0.0-1.0 ticks (2029.5 px per unit), z/H on the 0.0-0.4 ticks (2051 px per unit). Circles found by ring template matching (radius 10-12 px, 10 of 12 ring sectors dark, light centre), false hits on ticks and the U_m label removed, each assigned to the station whose DNS curve is nearest at the same height. The solid curves traced by a line follower after erasing the circles, from z = 0.48 to the wave surface. Accuracy about +-0.003 H in z and +-0.02 in u/Um_lower; in the dense near-wall clusters (stations 0.4, 0.7, 0.8) and where a circle lies on the curve some LDV points are missing (no circle is invented). The earlier version (morning of 6 Oct) joined a few points per station with straight lines and was wrong by up to 0.27 (station 0.7 at z = 0.1) and 0.84 (station 0.9 at z = 0.1).

fig6_variances.format: [eta/H, value]; sim_case4 every 0.005 H from the wall (0) to the top wall (1); exp_hudson (a dashed line in the paper, eta < 0.43) every 0.01 H
fig6_variances.note: Horizontal averages at constant eta. The paper does not say whether the fluctuations are about the phase average or about the plane average at constant eta; maass1994_plot.py uses the phase (x mod lambda), y and time average. Stray points from tick marks and labels removed on 6 Oct 2026 (a point more than 25 % of the range away from the median of its neighbours within 0.035 H).
fig6_variances.digitisation: Re-digitised 6 Oct 2026 at 600 dpi from the frame and tick calibration of each panel (u2, v2: 0-0.1; w2: 0-0.015; uw: -0.015-0.005 with the zero line). Solid curve traced row by row, the near-wall part column by column, Hudson's dashed line from the second stroke in each row, medians in 0.005/0.01 H bins. Accuracy about +-0.5 % of full scale; at eta < 0.01 the curves are drawn as reaching 0 at the wall.

fig7a_surface_pressure.quantity: 2 (P - P_ref) / (rho Um^2) along the lower wall, P_ref = P at the crest (x/lambda = 1)
fig7a_surface_pressure.note: Hudson's pressure was derived from the velocity field with a reference pressure near the channel centre (paper p. 294).

fig7b_momentum_flux.quantity: horizontally averaged vertical flux of downstream momentum, tau / Um^2, vs eta/H (case 4, t = 60)
